decisions.reason: A specialized agricultural crate with steady mentions has low holding cost in a broad portfolio, and harvest-crate demand is still unfolding, so the option stays open.
Its own dedicated page in both years signals strong commitment to a core foldable large-container line that fits the reusable logistics trend, so its value looks increasingly realized.
Stackable crates are a staple of the returnable packaging range with minimal incremental cost, so there is no evidence justifying abandonment.
A medium-duty rackable pallet fills a standard gap in the pallet range and costs little to maintain on existing tooling, so keeping the option is sensible.
Its move from a dedicated page to a mere mention suggests weaker prospects in a niche, but low holding costs and unresolved uncertainty favor keeping it for now.
Its reduced web presence hints at a modest result, yet as a pallet variant it shares production with the core range, so dropping it saves little until evidence turns clearly negative.
